packages.label: תְּפִלָּה וְתִקּוּן הַבְּרִית
packages.reason: All these concepts are parallel expressions of the same spiritual act: the directed, faithful outpouring of the soul toward God. The bow (keshet) is the tikkun habrit from which arrows (prayer) are shot. The three vavs (chai birchan d'tzluta) are the three blessings-of-prayer which are the arrows. The voice (kol), the hand (yad), faith (emunah), the daughter (bat), and blessings (berachot) are all bechinot of prayer — different facets of the same reaching-upward. Mashiach = Dibur (speech) = the very act of praying (mesiach ilmim). The Bow/Tikkun HaBrit is the structural enabling apparatus, identical in nature to prayer itself.

merge_notes.reason: The bow (keshet) IS the tikkun habrit — they share the same essential nature as the structural covenant-vessel that launches prayer. The proof text says 'תקון הברית שהוא קשת' directly identifying them. Merged into the Prayer package because the entire bow-and-arrow apparatus is a bechina of prayer itself.

Mashiach = Dibur (speech) = the faculty by which one prays (מֵשִׂיחַ אִלְּמִים — he who speaks the mute). The proof text explicitly states 'מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁהוּא הַדִּבּוּר שֶׁבּוֹ מִתְפַּלֵּל.' Mashiach-as-speech is the same reality as prayer/communication with God.

packages.label: שַׁבָּת וְתַכְלִית הַיְדִיעָה
packages.reason: These concepts all express the same transcendent domain: the holiness of Shabbat as the pinnacle of creation's wisdom. Kedushah shel Shabbat = Tachlit HaYediah (the ultimate knowing = knowing that we cannot know) = Mekomo Shel Olam (God as the Place that encompasses all). Shin = the three elements (fire, wind, water) that are the structural body of the word Shabbat (שַׁבָּת = שִׁין + בַּת), representing the three-dimensional holiness that fills creation. These are all faces of the same divine transcendence-that-encompasses-finitude.

merge_notes.reason: The letter Shin with its three branches = fire, wind, water. These are the first part of Shabbat (שַׁבָּת = שִׁין + בַּת). Shin represents the three-dimensional holiness of creation that Shabbat crowns. This small two-node component belongs to the Shabbat/Knowledge package because its proof text explicitly situates it inside the Shabbat word-analysis ('שַׁבָּת זוֹ שִׁין בַּת').

packages.label: גּוּף קָדוֹשׁ וּבִגְדֵי שַׁבָּת
packages.reason: Bigdei Shabbat (Shabbat garments) = Guf Kadosh m'Gan Eden (the holy body from the Garden of Eden) = Basar (flesh). These three concepts all name the same reality: the purified, holy body that a person receives after shedding the skin of the snake (mishkha d'chivya). 'Basar' in the verse 'bashar mibeshari' (flesh of my flesh) is the archetypal holy body. The Shabbat garments ARE that holy body — they are not clothes worn over a body but the holy body itself. The three are the same thing named from three angles.

packages.label: בּוּשָׁה וְכִסּוּי הַדָּם
packages.reason: All these concepts express the same redemptive spiritual mechanism: the purifying act of shame and its divine response. Bushah (shame) = Shefichat Damim (shedding of blood) = Shechitah (ritual slaughter) — the same act of humiliation that releases the life-force (blood) for purification. The Shechina's covering of Israel's spilled blood with love = Kisui Dam (blood covering) = the very mitzvot themselves (which are 'delicacies' the Holy One tastes). Neshamot HaNefulot (fallen souls) = Pesha'im (transgressions) — the 'material' that this covering transforms: what was sin becomes merit. Together they form one integrated domain: the path of shame-as-purification and divine love-as-covering.
nodes: שהשכינה מכסה דמהון של ישראל, שנשפך באהבה הזאת

merged_nodes: שהשכינה מכסה דמהון של ישראל, שנשפך באהבה הזאת
merge_notes.reason: Component E (Shechina's covering / kisui dam / mitzvot) shares the same nature as Component D (bushah / shechitah / shefichat damim): both describe the same purification act from complementary angles. Shechitah requires both cutting (= bushah/shefichat damim) and covering the blood (= kisui dam/Shechina's love). The mitzvot are the 'flesh' that God can taste once the shechitah-act of shame has been performed. These are not eitza (cause→effect) but two faces of the same sacrificial-atonement reality.

Component K belongs to the atonement domain: 'fallen souls are a bechina of transgressions' — they are the same spiritual 'substance' that the kisui dam/love covers and elevates. The falling souls ARE the pesha'im in their unredeemed form; after covering they become zechuyot. They share the same essential nature as the 'material of atonement' that this package addresses.

packages.label: מַיִם רַבִּים וְזֶרַע מְרֵעִים
packages.label_en: Many Waters and Evil Seed — External Destructive Forces
packages.reason: These four concepts all represent the same domain: the external evil forces that try to destroy Israel's holiness. Mayim Rabbim (many waters) = Ahavot vYirot Chitzoniyot (external loves and fears) — the spiritual forces that try to drown and extinguish the holy fire of Torah. Zera Mereim (evil seed) = Mei HaMabul (Flood waters) — the destructive seed-force that seeks to overwhelm Israel, identical in nature to the primordial destructive deluge. Both pairs are 'evil water' — drowning, extinguishing, flooding forces that oppose the covenant.

merge_notes.reason: Components F (זרע מרעים/מי המבול) and G (מים רבים/אהבות ויראות חיצוניות) both represent the same evil domain: external water-forces that try to extinguish, overwhelm, or pollute Israel's holiness. The Rebbe identifies all of them as the opposing force to the holy fire of Torah-love. They are two expressions of the same evil — 'raging external waters' — sharing essential nature as the anti-covenant flood.
